The immediate goal is to strip out all HTML tags before applying the `substr()` function, ensuring you only count visible characters and not the length of closing brackets. ### Why Simple Regex Fails The most instinctive solution for many developers is to reach for a regular expression. You might try using `preg_replace` with a pattern like `/<.*?>/` to strip tags. However, this approach is notoriously fragile in real-world scenarios. HTML tags can nest (e.g., `
text

Furthermore, relying on regex to parse HTML violates the principle of using the right tool for the job. It is not designed for structural parsing. If your goal is just to strip tags for display purposes in PHP, the `strip_tags()` function exists specifically for this and handles the vast majority of standard cases more reliably than a custom regular expression. ### Using `strip_tags()` Correctly The built-in `strip_tags()` function removes all HTML and PHP tags from a string.
